lines.japanese: 休憩時間が終わると、俺はまたスタッフルームへ戻って地道にマニュアルを読みはじめました。
lines.english: When my break ended, I returned to the staff room and resumed my patient progress through the manual.

lines.japanese: キッチン担当の先輩スタッフ（同年代の男子数人）も、それぞれの休憩時間にはこちらへ上がっていらして、俺は彼らと軽いおしゃべりを交わすことができました。
lines.english: The more experienced kitchen crew—several men around my age—came upstairs for their respective breaks, giving me the chance to exchange a little casual conversation with them.

lines.japanese: 初日なのであまり出しゃばった態度は見せず、彼ら好みの話の方向性みたいなのを探りながら、まあ無難にやり過ごせたんじゃないかと思います。
lines.english: Since it was my first day, I kept myself from coming on too strong and felt out what kinds of conversation each of them preferred. I think I made it through safely enough.

lines.japanese: もっとも最初なんてのはいつだってわりと簡単な方で、難しいのはこの距離をこの温度で維持しつづけることなんですよね。
lines.english: Of course, the beginning was always the relatively easy part. The difficulty lay in maintaining that exact distance at that exact temperature.

lines.japanese: 閉店時間の一時間前になると、マスターからの内線電話で一階へ呼ばれました。
lines.english: One hour before closing, an internal call from the boss summoned me downstairs.

lines.japanese: 千歳鷲介は、今後もこのあたりの時間を潮に、クローズと呼ばれる閉店準備作業へ配置が換わるのだそうです。
lines.english: In future, this would generally be the point when Shusuke Chitose switched to closing duties—the “close.”

lines.japanese: したがってこの時間からは、俺の担当トレーナーも玉泉先輩から、その作業に明るいべつの男子スタッフへと一時交替です。
lines.english: Accordingly, from this hour onward Tamaizumi would temporarily hand my training over to another male employee who knew the closing routine.

lines.japanese: 「オールダウンしてから遅くても二十分で帰りたいんだ。そのつもりで働いてもらえる？」
lines.english: “Once everything's shut down, we want to be out of here within twenty minutes at the latest. Can you work with that in mind?”

lines.japanese: 工藤さんと名乗った黒ブチ眼鏡の先輩は、大きな声と意味のない手振りが特徴の大学三年生でした。
lines.english: Kudo, a third-year university student in black-rimmed glasses, was distinguished by a loud voice and meaningless hand gestures.

lines.japanese: 「閉店時間は１０時だけど、要はそれまでに、洗えるものはどんどん洗っちゃうのね。で、客がいなくなったらすぐにフロアの方の片付け」
lines.english: “We close at ten, but basically, wash everything you can before then. Once the customers are gone, start clearing the dining room immediately.”

lines.japanese: 「ちんたらやってると一時間ぐらいかかるんだけど、コツ掴んで一気にやっちゃえば……そうね、平日ならだいたい１０時１５分には終わるかなぁ」
lines.english: “If you dawdle, it can take an hour. Once you get the knack and knock it all out at once... well, on a weekday we're generally done by ten fifteen.”

lines.japanese: 食器や調理器具の洗浄、店内の清掃、ゴミ出しなどを、無計画な順番で次々に説明していくので、俺は頭が混乱しそうでした。あとでメモにまとめておく必要がありそうです。
lines.english: He explained washing dishes and cooking utensils, cleaning the restaurant, taking out the garbage, and one task after another in no discernible order. My head nearly spun. I would need to organize it all into notes later.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、今日は初めてだから、多少時間かかっても仕方ないけどさ。でも慣れれば掃除もわりとテキトーんなってくるし、早番のおばちゃんに押しつけときゃいい作業とか、そういうのだんだん分かってくるから」
lines.english: “It's your first day, so taking a little longer can't be helped. Once you get used to it, though, the cleaning gets pretty slapdash. You learn which jobs you can leave for the older women on the opening shift.”

lines.japanese: 「今日は俺と千歳君だけだけど、日によってはもうひとりふたり増えたりもするし、そういうときはだいぶ早く帰れるよ」
lines.english: “It's only you and me tonight, but some days we have another one or two people. Then we can leave much earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「工藤さんはご自宅遠いんですか？」
lines.english: “Do you live far away, Kudo?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、チャリ１０分。え、なんで？」
lines.english: “No, ten minutes by bike. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いえ、随分と時間を気にされてるようだったんで」
lines.english: “Oh, no. You simply seemed rather concerned about the time.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、聞いてない？　うち１０時以降はサービス残業だよ。金出ないのに真面目にやったって意味ないでしょ」
lines.english: “Nobody told you? After ten, it's unpaid overtime here. There's no point working seriously once they stop paying us.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なるほど、合理的ですね」
lines.english: “Ah. I see. Very rational.”

lines.japanese: 俺は深々と頷いてみせたけど、笑いかえすことはしませんでした。
lines.english: I gave him a deep nod, but did not return his smile.

lines.japanese: そして──閉店作業が終わったのは１０時３０分過ぎでした。
lines.english: And so—we finished closing sometime after ten thirty.

lines.japanese: 工藤さんはスポーティーなごつい腕時計を見下ろして「次からはもちっと急ごうな」とおっしゃいました。
lines.english: Kudo looked down at his chunky sports watch and said, “Let's pick it up a little next time.”

lines.japanese: 体を動かす作業はちょっと疲れたけど、ようやく“働いてる”実感を得ることができたので、それはそれで良かったと思います。
lines.english: The physical work had tired me somewhat, but at last I felt as though I had actually worked. That, at least, was gratifying.

lines.japanese: 着替えるためにスタッフルームへ戻ると、私服姿の日和子さんと鉢合わせました。
lines.english: When I returned to the staff room to change, I ran into Hiyoko in her everyday clothes.

lines.japanese: あれ、私服……？
lines.english: Wait. Street clothes...?

lines.japanese: 来るときは制服だったはずなのに……まあ、どうでもいいか。
lines.english: Hadn't she arrived in uniform...? Well, it hardly mattered.

lines.japanese: <8>\「お疲れさまです！」
lines.english: “Hey! Done for the night?”

lines.japanese: 「お疲れさまでした」
lines.english: “Yes. Good night.”

lines.japanese: 俺はフレッシュマンらしく腰を９０度に折って溌剌とした挨拶をしました。日和子さんはさらりと応えて、なんら惜しむこともなく新人の横を通りすぎていきました。
lines.english: Like any fresh-faced newcomer, I bent a crisp ninety degrees at the waist and offered a vigorous greeting. Hiyoko answered lightly and passed me without a hint of reluctance at leaving the rookie behind.

lines.japanese: 「あー！　えーと、あの日和子さん！」
lines.english: “Ah! Um, Hiyoko!”

lines.japanese: 思わず言葉が足りないような気がして呼びとめてしまいました。
lines.english: Feeling somehow that the exchange was missing something, I called her back without thinking.

lines.japanese: 彼女はあの直線的な動作で、声も表情もなく、ひらりと振りかえりました。
lines.english: With that characteristically straight-line motion, she wheeled lightly around, bringing neither voice nor expression with her.

lines.japanese: 「や、その、なんですか──」
lines.english: “Well, I mean—”

lines.japanese: 「──ああ、そうそう。玉泉トレーナー、今日は一日ありがとうございました！」
lines.english: “—Oh, right. Coach Tamaizumi, thank you for everything today!”

lines.japanese: おちゃらけで敬礼なんてしてみると、日和子さんは真顔でじっと俺の目を見てから言いました。
lines.english: I tried a playful salute. Hiyoko looked gravely into my eyes for a long moment before answering.

lines.japanese: 「礼には及びません。仕事ですから」
lines.english: “There is no need to thank me. It is my job.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、明日もよろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “See you tomorrow!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。明日もいらっしゃるんですか」
lines.english: “Oh. You're coming tomorrow too?”

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめんなさい！　よろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry! See you tomorrow!”

lines.japanese: 「はい。それではお先に失礼します」
lines.english: “Very well. Good night, then.”

lines.japanese: 「あ！　自分ももう上がるんすけど、あの日和子さん、もし良かったら駅まで──」
lines.english: “Wait! I'm finishing too, so, Hiyoko, if you'd like, we could walk to the station—”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: あからさまに俺の言葉を遮って口を開いた日和子さん。
lines.english: Hiyoko opened her mouth, very plainly cutting me off.

lines.japanese: 「先ほども申しあげましたけど、ええ、お持ちいただいて結構ですから」
lines.english: “As I said earlier, yes, you're quite welcome to take it with you.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は四本の指先を揃え、（俺から見て）右手を指しました。その先にあるものは──ぴったり閉まったキャビネットのガラス戸に『従業員規則と心構え』の背表紙。
lines.english: She held four fingertips neatly together and pointed to her right—my left. At the end of the gesture, behind the cabinet's tightly shut glass door, waited the spine of *Employee Rules and Professional Conduct*.

lines.japanese: 「……き、機会があれば」
lines.english: “...I-if the opportunity arises.”

lines.japanese: 俺はあとずさって答えました。
lines.english: I answered while retreating.

lines.japanese: 「失礼いたします」
lines.english: “Good night.”

lines.japanese: その隙を突いて、日和子さんはひとりで去っていきました。
lines.english: Seizing the opening, Hiyoko left by herself.

lines.japanese: 「しょっぼーん」
lines.english: “Cue the sad trombone.”

lines.japanese: 「あらー、ふられちゃったねー」
lines.english: “Oh, dear. She turned you down.”

lines.japanese: 「いやおまえ、イタリア人じゃねーんだから初日からがっつくなよ」
lines.english: “You're not Italian. Don't come on so strong on your first day.”

lines.japanese: 「まーまー、明日があるさ明後日もあるさー」
lines.english: “Now, now. There's always tomorrow. And the day after.”

lines.japanese: 「せ、先輩方……いつの間に……」
lines.english: “Y-you two... When did you get here...?”

lines.japanese: おふたりの背後を見れば、さっき閉まっていた更衣室のドアが、いまはぱっくり口を開けていました。
lines.english: Behind the two women, the changing-room door that had been closed a moment ago now yawned wide.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、着替えてたんすか……」
lines.english: “Oh, you were changing...”

lines.japanese: 「あの服のまま通勤してたら田舎の両親泣いちゃうよ」
lines.english: “My parents back in the country would weep if I commuted in that outfit.”

lines.japanese: 「つかさー、三人揃って更衣室入ったのに、ひとりだけソッコー着替えて出てくとかってどーなのよ」
lines.english: “Still, the three of us went into the changing room together, and one of us changed at warp speed and marched straight out. What's with that?”

lines.japanese: 「えりちゃんが意地悪なことばっかり言うからさー」
lines.english: “Because you kept saying mean things to her, Eriko.”

lines.japanese: 「まーた紀奈子さんは私ばっか悪もんにしてー。本来なら最年長の役割っすよー、たまひよの教育ー」
lines.english: “There you go, making me the villain again. Reeducating Tama-chick should really be the oldest woman's job.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さんの悪い癖でしょソレ、言うべきこと言わないで笑ってごまかすっつーの。いまは可愛いからいいけど、歳喰ってそんなんしてたら殴られるかんねー」
lines.english: “That's your bad habit, Kinako. You never say what needs saying; you just laugh and smooth it over. It's cute now, but keep that up when you're old and somebody'll punch you.”

lines.japanese: 「えりちゃん、ひどーい！　千歳君、言いかえしてよう！」
lines.english: “Eriko, that's awful! Shusuke, tell her off!”

lines.japanese: 「こら英里子」
lines.english: “Now listen here, Eriko.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「まったくおまえは、いつもいつも、ひとのことばかり文句つけおって。いつまでもそんな風だとな、おまえの……えーと、なんか欠点とかをずばり指摘しちゃうゾ☆」
lines.english: “Honestly, all you ever do is criticize other people. If you keep this up, I'm going to... um, call out some personal flaw of yours with devastating accuracy. So there☆”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジで？　いいよ、言ってよ、ずばり指摘してよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Go ahead. Point one out with devastating accuracy.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんの罠だっぺ……」
lines.english: “Wh-what kind of trap is this...?”

lines.japanese: 予想外の反応に、俺と紀奈子さんは身を寄せあってぶるぶる震えあがりました。
lines.english: Faced with that unforeseen response, Kinako and I huddled together and trembled.

lines.japanese: 「い、いや英里子さん、やめた方がいいっすよ。実は俺、かなり辛口っすから。かなりカプサイシンっすよ。ハバネロトークでアナタの心を引きさきますよ」
lines.english: “N-now, Eriko, perhaps you should reconsider. I'm an extremely harsh critic. Pure capsaicin. I'll tear your heart apart with habanero-grade criticism.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、おまえ聞くけどさ、電車とかで気付かないうちにファスナー全開ってなってるとき──」
lines.english: “Then answer me this. Say your fly comes open on the train without you noticing—”

lines.japanese: 英里子さんは俺の股ぐらを顎で指しました。
lines.english: Miss Hino indicated my crotch with her chin.

lines.japanese: 「知らねーやつら大勢にげらげら笑われっぱなしなのと、仲いいやつひとりに『バカ開いてるよ』って言われんのと、どっちがマシだと思う？」
lines.english: “Would you rather have a whole crowd of strangers laughing at you, or one friend lean over and say, ‘Idiot, your fly's open’?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。素敵な痴女にそっと指を挿しいれていただくのがいいです」
lines.english: “I'd prefer a ravishing pervert to slip one gentle finger inside.”

lines.japanese: 「てか、私思うんだけどさー」
lines.english: “See, here's what I think—”

lines.japanese: 軽部狩男のもとで働いている英里子さんに、下品な茶化しは通用しませんでした。
lines.english: Having worked under Karuo Karube, Miss Hino was impervious to vulgar deflection.

lines.japanese: 「知らないとこで陰口叩かれるぐらいだったら、直接言われた方がナンボか良くない？」
lines.english: “Wouldn't you rather hear criticism to your face than have people talk behind your back?”

lines.japanese: 「だってさあ、人間だったらぜったい自分で気付かない欠点ってあるわけじゃん。私だったら、そーゆーのはむしろ教えてもらいたいけどねえ？」
lines.english: “I mean, everyone’s got flaws they’d never notice on their own, right? Me, I’d rather have someone tell me about that stuff.”

lines.japanese: ふうん……。
lines.english: Hmm...

lines.japanese: まあ、たしかにその例えは頷ける。なるほど、いつも言いたい放題言いまくりの英里子さんには、言いたい放題言いまくる英里子さんなりの哲学があったのか。
lines.english: I had to admit, the analogy made sense. So Eriko, who always said whatever she pleased to whomever she pleased, had a philosophy all her own about saying whatever she pleased.

lines.japanese: 「ま、言われたとこで直すかどうかは分かんないけど」
lines.english: “Not that I promise to fix anything you point out.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、直してくださいよ」
lines.english: “No, please fix it.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、じゃあねー、えりちゃんの欠点はー……」
lines.english: “Hmm. In that case, Eriko's flaw is...”

lines.japanese: 「お、なんだ。よし来い」
lines.english: “Oh? All right, let's hear it.”

lines.japanese: 「言葉きっついこと」
lines.english: “Your words are too harsh.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめ、それは直んない」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. That one isn't changing.”

lines.japanese: 「諦めんの早っ！」
lines.english: “You gave up instantly!”

lines.japanese: 「てゆか、それは言われなくても自覚してるし。デメリットよりメリットのが多いし。直す意味がない」
lines.english: “Besides, I already know that. It has more benefits than drawbacks. There's no point changing it.”

lines.japanese: 「さ、さようですか」
lines.english: “I-I see.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、他にはー？」
lines.english: “What else?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、他も何も、アナタの困りどころはすべてその一点に集束されますから」
lines.english: “There is no ‘else.’ Every difficulty you present converges upon that single point.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　あんだろ、他にも叩きどころがよー。おめ遠慮してんじゃねーよ、なんか気付いたこと言ってくれってー」
lines.english: “What? There've got to be other things to tear into me for. Don't hold back. Tell me anything you've noticed.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、何この絡み方！　タチ悪っ！　打ち上げ三次会あたりのバンド少年みたい！」
lines.english: “God, what is this routine? You're like a guy in a band three after-parties deep!”

lines.japanese: 「や、ていうかですね？　英里子さんのことなら俺なんかよりも、付き合いの深い紀奈子さんの方がよくご存知だと思いますよ？　ええ、絡むならぜひあちらに」
lines.english: “Actually, you know what? Kinako has known you much longer than I have. She must understand you far better. Please direct all further aggression toward her.”

lines.japanese: 「あーうん、じゃあ今度、時間があったら考えとくさ」
lines.english: “Oh, sure. I'll think about it next time I have a spare minute.”

lines.japanese: 「マジでー。紀奈子さん、いつも面倒かけて悪いね」
lines.english: “Seriously? Sorry I'm always such a bother, Kinako.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、よかっぺよー」
lines.english: “Mm, no trouble at all.”

lines.japanese: うわあ、さすが紀奈子さんだあ。
lines.english: Wow. That was Kinako for you.

lines.japanese: 「それでは！　お疲れさまでした！」
lines.english: “Well, then! Good night!”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なに千歳、まだ帰んないの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Chitose, aren't you leaving yet?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、駅まで一緒に行こうよ」
lines.english: “Come on, walk to the station with us.”

lines.japanese: 「んまあ、誰かさんと違ってなんて嬉しいお言葉──や、ところが残念なことに、ワタクシちょっと生理現象が」
lines.english: “My, what delightful words, unlike a certain somebody's. Unfortunately, a minor biological necessity calls.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、便所？」
lines.english: “Oh, the toilet?”

lines.japanese: 「えりちゃん、女の子なんだからもうちょっと言葉選ぼうよー」
lines.english: “Eriko, you're a girl. Choose your words a little more carefully.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、お便所？」
lines.english: “Then... the little toilet?”

lines.japanese: 「お手洗いとかー」
lines.english: “How about ‘restroom’?”

lines.japanese: 「あっひゃっひゃっひゃっ！　腹いてー！」
lines.english: “Ah-hya-hya-hya! My stomach hurts!”

lines.japanese: 「え……私、いま面白いこと言った？」
lines.english: “What...? Did I just say something funny?”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、とりあえずいいコンビだと思いますよ、アレックス２」
lines.english: “Well, I can at least say you make an excellent comedy duo, Alex Two.”

lines.japanese: 「千歳、トイレだろ。いいよほら、うちら待ってるからダッシュでしてこいよ」
lines.english: “Chitose, you need the toilet, right? Fine, we'll wait. Run along and get it over with.”

lines.japanese: 「や、ホントありがたいんすけどね。すいません、ちょっと長引きそうなんで」
lines.english: “I really appreciate it, but I'm sorry. This may take a while.”

lines.japanese: 「え、だいじょぶ？　おなか壊しちゃった？」
lines.english: “Are you all right? Stomach trouble?”

lines.japanese: 「ああいえいえ、全然。普通に」
lines.english: “Oh, no, no. Nothing like that. Perfectly normal.”

lines.japanese: 「普通になんだよ。おめ、店のトイレでいかがわしーことすんなよ」
lines.english: “Normal what? Don't do anything filthy in the restaurant bathroom.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それだ。英里子さんの欠点は、発想が狩男的なことだ」
lines.english: “That's it. Miss Hino's flaw is that her mind works like Karuo's.”

lines.japanese: 「うぇー、マジでー。それは直すわ。ソッコー直すわ」
lines.english: “Ugh, seriously? I'm fixing that. Right now.”

lines.japanese: 「はい。お願いします」
lines.english: “Please do.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、また明日だね千歳くん。ばいばーい」
lines.english: “See you tomorrow, Shusuke. Bye!”

lines.japanese: 「おつー」
lines.english: “Later.”

lines.japanese: 「お休みなさぁ～い！」
lines.english: “Good niiiight!”
“…Phew.”

lines.japanese: ふたりを見送って時刻を確認。
lines.english: After seeing the two of them off, I checked the time.

lines.japanese: あらら、１０時半を２０分ほど過ぎちゃってますね。
lines.english: Goodness. It was already twenty minutes past ten thirty.

lines.japanese: ま、いっかあ！
lines.english: Ah, who cared!

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どうした鷲介、おまえ、望月君たちと帰ったんじゃなかったのか」
lines.english: “Hm? What are you still doing here, Shusuke? I thought you left with Miss Mochizuki and the others.”

lines.japanese: 「ええまあ、ちょっとお手洗いを借りていこうと思いまして」
lines.english: “Well, I thought I'd use the bathroom before I went.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか。きょう一日の艶めかしい記憶が消えないうちに、いかがわしいことを済ませておくのか」
lines.english: “Ah, I see. You mean to take care of your dirty business while today's sensual memories are still fresh.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、も、ほんと発言が期待を裏切らないっすねマスター」
lines.english: “Wow. You really never disappoint, do you, boss?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、人間なんて期待されているうちが華だからな」
lines.english: “Well, a man is only in his prime as long as people still expect something of him.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、皆さんアナタにはいつまでも期待してると思いますよ」
lines.english: “Oh, I think everyone will go on expecting that of you forever.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん。嬉しいことを言ってくれるじゃないか。ペーパーなら存分に使っていいぞ」
lines.english: “Hmph. How gratifying. You may use as much toilet paper as you require.”

lines.japanese: 「うゎお！　お気持ちだけで！」
lines.english: “Wow! The thought is more than enough!”

lines.japanese: ふ～う、っと……。
lines.english: Phewww...

lines.japanese: はあ……やっぱりここは落ちつくねえ……。
lines.english: Ah... This place really did settle the nerves...

lines.japanese: さて。
lines.english: Now, then.

lines.japanese: 便座に腰掛けたまま、スポーツバッグから安物の手帳を取りだします。
lines.english: Still seated on the toilet, I pulled a cheap planner from my sports bag.

lines.japanese: これを見た米田さんは「このデジタル時代になんてアナクロな」などとおっしゃいましたが、いやいや、なかなかどうして紙には紙の良さがあるもんですよ。
lines.english: When Yoneda saw it, she called me hopelessly anachronistic in the digital age. But no, no—paper had virtues entirely its own.

lines.japanese: 古代エジプトのパピルスを祖とする、四千年超の歴史は伊達じゃないってなもんで。
lines.english: Four thousand years of history descending from the papyrus of ancient Egypt were nothing to sneeze at.

lines.japanese: 手帳に挿されていた細くて短いボールペンを手に、俺は俺のきょう一日を頭から早送りで回想しました（もちろんマスターの言ったような意味ではなく）。
lines.english: Taking the short, slender ballpoint pen tucked inside the planner, I replayed the entire day at high speed inside my head—naturally, not in the sense the boss had suggested.

lines.japanese: ん、まあ、疲れたけど悪くない日だったかな。
lines.english: Hmm. Tiring, certainly, but perhaps not a bad day.

lines.japanese: 日記を付けてるわけじゃないんですけど、ほら、覚えておいた方がいいこととかね、あるでしょ。習ったばかりの作業内容とか、いつか米田さんからの仕事で使えそうなネタとか、その他連絡事項とか。
lines.english: It wasn't as though I kept a diary. Still, there were things worth remembering, weren't there? Procedures I had just learned, material that might someday prove useful in work for Yoneda, and various other notes.

lines.japanese: 最後に俺は、手帳のお尻の方のページへ飛んで、「今日からアレキサンダーでバイトを始めました」で始まる短い一文を書きなぐりました。
lines.english: Finally, I flipped to a page near the back of the planner and scrawled a short sentence beginning, “Today I started working at Alexander.”

lines.japanese: ぐり、ぐり、と文末にハートマークを添えて完成。
lines.english: Scritch, scritch. A heart at the end completed it.

lines.japanese: びっ、とそのページをちぎってから、ちょっと遠くへ離して読みなおし。
lines.english: I tore out the page with a sharp rip, held it a little farther away, and read it again.

lines.japanese: んー……。
lines.english: Hmm...

lines.japanese: そのまま手の中でくしゃりと握りつぶして、ゆっくり目を閉じました。
lines.english: Then I crumpled it in my hand and slowly closed my eyes.

lines.japanese: さて……まあ……用も済ませたし？
lines.english: Well... now, then... My business here was finished, wasn't it?

lines.japanese: 帰りますかね。
lines.english: Time to head home, I suppose.

lines.japanese: おやすみ。
lines.english: Good night.
